question: The excavated ruins of the Nalanda University indicate that bright red _____ was/were used in its construction.
solution:
The correct answer is __**bricks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ruins of Nalanda University, located in Bihar, India, predominantly exhibit the use of bright red bricks in their construction.
 
• The use of bricks was a common practice in ancient Indian architecture due to their availability and durability.
 
• The bricks used in Nalanda were typically made from locally sourced clay, which was shaped and fired to create a robust building material.
 
• Many of the structures, including classrooms, monasteries, and stupas, were constructed using these bricks, which have withstood the test of time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nalanda University**

 
 
• Founded in the 5th century CE during the Gupta Dynasty.
 
• It was one of the first residential universities in the world, housing over 10,000 students and 2,000 teachers.
 
• Renowned for its diverse curriculum that included Buddhist studies, fine arts, medicine, mathematics, and more.
 
• It attracted students from various regions, including China, Korea, Japan, Tibet, Mongolia, Turkey, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **Ancient Indian Architecture**
 
 
• Utilized materials like brick, stone, and wood depending on regional availability.
 
• Known for its intricate carvings, detailed sculptures, and sophisticated urban planning.
 
• Prominent examples include the rock-cut caves of Ajanta and Ellora, the temples of Khajuraho, and the city planning of Mohenjo-daro.
 
• Architecture often had religious significance, with many structures serving as temples, monasteries, or stupas.
 
 
 
• **Brickmaking Techniques**
 
 
• Involved sourcing clay, molding it into shape, and firing it in a kiln to harden.
 
• Different regions developed distinct styles and sizes of bricks.
 
• In ancient India, bricks were often sun-dried before being fired for additional strength.
 
• The durability of bricks made them a preferred choice for long-lasting constructions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nalanda**
 
 
• Nalanda was a major center of learning and intellectual exchange in ancient India.
 
• It played a critical role in the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• The university's library, known as Dharma Gunj, was one of the largest and most comprehensive of its time.
 
• Excavations have revealed extensive ruins that provide insight into ancient academic life and architecture.
